title: Quantifier elimination: equality patterns and dense orders
summary: Remove quantifiers from equality and dense-order formulas, then describe their definable sets and elementary inclusions.
abstract: In the rational order, asking whether there is a point strictly between two given points is the same as asking whether the first is smaller than the second. Quantifier elimination extends this simplification to every formula of a theory. For infinite sets with equality alone, formulas reduce to equality comparisons; for nonempty dense linear orders without endpoints, they reduce to comparisons of order and equality. This determines which subsets formulas can describe: finite or cofinite sets in the first case, and finite unions of intervals and points in the second, with parameters allowed. It also shows that all models of each theory agree on sentences, and inclusions between its models preserve every formula with parameters.
